key_insight: Well-calibrated large language models can act as low-cost statistical estimators that achieve Bayes-optimal risk for inference tasks determined only by conditional means under squared loss.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical substitute for expensive human-subject experiments in some prediction and decision-making pipelines, reducing cost and latency when scope conditions are met.
method: Model the LLM as a misspecified functional estimator trained on i.i.d. data.
Decompose error into representation bias and optimization error, then bound the asymptotic risk.
Use bidirectional Le Cam deficiency analysis and calibration rules to certify restricted functional risk equivalence.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical risk decomposition, finite-sample concentration bounds, and a calibration protocol, with performance characterized against Bayes-optimal squared-loss risk rather than a single empirical dataset.
watch_item: The guarantee is restricted to well-calibrated models and inference that depends only on the conditional mean, so identifiability and representation bias can still inflate the risk floor outside those conditions.
paper_title: Using Large Language Models as Low-Cost Statistical Estimators for Human-Response Data
